prompt: Some schools teach children of all abilities together in the same class, while others divide students into groups according to how well they perform. Discuss both approaches and give your own opinion.
essay:
Most of the damage attributed to ability grouping is not caused by the grouping. It is caused by the way schools assign children to groups and then decline to move them. A set allocated at eleven on the basis of a single test, taught a narrower curriculum by less experienced staff and revisited once a year at most, is not really a teaching arrangement at all; it is a prediction that arranges for its own fulfilment.

The practical case for setting deserves more respect than it usually gets. A teacher facing a class whose attainment spans four years has three options, all bad: aim at the middle and lose both ends, prepare three parallel lessons for one room, or let the strongest students spend a term revisiting what they already know. In subjects that build strictly on what came before, this is not a matter of preference. A student who cannot manipulate fractions will not learn algebra by sitting in a lesson about algebra, and no amount of good intention alters that.

The objection to sorting, though, is not really about pedagogy either. Attainment at eleven correlates heavily with how much reading happened at home, so a system that sorts early is partly sorting by background while telling children it has measured their ability. That message is the injury, and it is administered by the label rather than by the teaching. A child who understands themselves to be in the group that is not expected to progress will, with remarkable consistency, stop expecting it too.

Both views therefore describe something true, and the argument between them is less important than a third thing neither mentions. Group where the subject is genuinely cumulative and teach together where it is not; but make the groups small, temporary and frequently reassessed, put the most capable teachers with the students furthest behind, and ensure that moving up is a routine event rather than an exception. Setting done that way is a timetable. Done the usual way, it is a verdict.
title: Mixed-ability classes or setting by ability
